subject: Private GPU orchestration: surge containment & throughput governance
messages:
From: Samuel Park <sam.park@edgecorp.io>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput targets & surge containment for EdgeCorp private pool

Rishi —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We're moving fast on a private VPC deployment and need to lock the throughput targets and a surge containment approach before procurement signs off. Key asks from our side:

- Target sustained throughput: 150k tokens/min across mixed model workload (chat + embedding rerank)
- Peak burst tolerance: 450k tokens/min for short windows (~3–5m) with graceful degradation after 10m
- Warm pool lead time and cold-start amortization: what to budget for initial ramping
- Network egress bounds and any cross-AZ caveats for our on-prem colocations

Can you send a short sizing proposal and a mutual action plan we can attach to the SOW? If possible include a run-rate spreadsheet and a simple network diagram we can hand to our infra team.

Thanks — Sam
Samuel Park
Head of Platform Engineering, EdgeCorp
sam.park@edgecorp.io

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput targets & surge containment for EdgeCorp private pool

Sam —

Appreciate the clear asks. High-level answers up front, detailed proposal attached:

1) Sustained throughput: we recommend reserving a baseline pool sized for 180k tokens/min to provide a 20% safety buffer against variance in workload mix. That maps to ~16 x A100-equivalent units (config details in the sheet).

2) Burst handling: design a warm pool that can absorb a 3x spike (450k tokens/min) for 5 minutes. For sustained bursts >10m we propose automatic admission control that evicts non-critical batches and falls back to a slightly smaller model variant to protect tail latency.

3) Warmup & cold start: warm-pool capacity should be kept at ~18% of committed capacity during business hours; cold-start amortization measured in minutes (3–7m depending on model KV cache). We'll provide a recommended ramp schedule.

4) Networking: cross-AZ egress is fine with private peering; recommend dedicate 40Gbps egress headroom to start and enable link-level policing to avoid saturation storms. Detailed NIC oversubscription guidance in the diagram.

Next steps: I attached a two-tab workbook (runrate & sizing) and a draft mutual action plan. If that looks good we'll schedule a call next week with procurement to lock lead times and the SOW.

Attaching: runrate_model_v1.xlsx, MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_EdgeCorp.docx, privgpu_network_diagram.png

— Rishi

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 16 Jun 2028 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: EdgeCorp sizing review + operational constraints

Folks —

Looping you in so we can align on the proposal details before I send the final sizing plan to EdgeCorp. Important constraints from their note: sustained 150k tokens/min, 3–5m 450k bursts, business hours ramp behavior. Draft recommendations (see attached sheet):

- Commit baseline: size for 180k tokens/min to give ~20% buffer. This maps to 16 A100-equivalent workers with continuous-batching at target latencies (p99 < 250ms for chat, p50 < 120ms for rerank embeddings).

- Warm-pool mechanics: maintain a warm pool equivalent to ~18% of capacity (3 workers) during peak hours. Warm pools should run lighter-weight models pinned to reduce KV cache churn.

- Admission control: implement the following staged policies — (1) soft throttle non-critical jobs (batch lower-priority traffic) at 1.5x baseline; (2) transparent model downgrade for heavy queries after 8m of sustained overage; (3) emergency fallback to hosted read-only endpoints if local capacity > 20% over threshold for 15m.

- Network & egress: require 40Gbps per-rack headroom. Also recommend link-level ingress policing and a per-tenant egress metering token so we can enforce graceful shedding rather than TCP-level drops. Note: cross-AZ latency has degraded recovery window by ~30s in our simulations.

- Observability: add token-level cost traces and KV-cache hit-rate dashboards; include a scheduled daily runbook check for warm-pool occupancy and cache warmness.

Open questions for the SOW/procurement:
- Procurement wants deterministic lead times for additional capacity; what is our stated ramp SLA for adding +4 workers (best effort vs committed)?
- What does pricing look like for cold-start-heavy workloads (they expect a ramp month where traffic is 2x planned).

Irene/Laura — can you confirm the thermal / power budgets for adding workers in a colocated rack? Marissa — can you sanity-check the admission-control thresholds and fallback play?

Thanks,
Rishi

Rishi / team —

Thanks — the baseline + warm-pool approach looks reasonable and matches our risk appetite. A few operational asks before we move to procurement:

1) Can you add a short clause to the mutual action plan that guarantees a 7-business-day lead time for adding up to +4 worker units once purchase is approved? We can accept "best effort" for larger increments but need a guaranteed short lead for quick absorption.
2) Please include the network diagram in our SOW attachment and flag the 40Gbps recommendation explicitly.
3) We'll run a 2-week soak with 1.8x traffic before go-live; can you provide an estimated additional cost during that soak so procurement can budget?

If you can update the doc and HubSpot record, procurement will open the PO next week. Also please Cc our Ops contact (ops@avasys.com) on the SOW.

I'll schedule a procurement sync for Tue.
